newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Tuesday, Oct 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Tuesday, Oct 2.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* French President Jacques Chirac triggered a diplomatic row with Rome by casting doubts on whether Italy would be among the first group of countries joining the single currency. Chirac then rowed back saying he ardently hopes Italy will succeed in joining the first EMU group. A (all).
* Prime minister Romano Prodi says some European partners are motivated by fear of competition fron dynamic Italian industry "We'll show them....Italy has extraordinary initiative skills" (all).
* Trade unions and Communist Refoundation party leader Fausto Bertinotti want to soften the 1997 budget and asks for revision of new housing tax (Corriere).

* Fiat chairman Cesare Romiti says the 1997 budget is "certainly heavy and above all unbalanced in terms of fiscal revenues". "A legal bribe, the most shocking of all" weighs on Italian revenues (all).

* Olivetti lost another 6.5 pct at the Milan stock exchange, as group debts almost doubled in July and August. Stock exchange watchdog Consob is examining a report from internal auditors over the group financial statements (Corriere della Sera, Sole 24 Ore).
* Labour costs for bigger companies grew by 6.2 pct in the first half of 1996. The employment rate slipped 1 pct in the industry sector and 2 pct in services (Sole 24 Ore).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
